description: Full-state-space semantic specification for the Infinite Ping-Pong actor system: one logical Ping and one logical Pong exchange a single protocol token forever.

semantic_backend.reason: The defining property is positive recurrence. A counterexample-only trace cannot establish that the request/reply protocol returns to an equivalent operational state.

source_note.namespace_artifact: The supplied source declares PingMessage, PongMessage, and StartMessage in InfiniteExample but references s1_simpleExample.* in handlers and startup. The semantic contract treats these as the logical Start, Ping, and Pong message roles and does not require the target to preserve the package qualifier.

observable_protocol.startup: The initialized system automatically triggers Ping, which emits exactly one initial request to Pong.
observable_protocol.pong_behavior: When Pong consumes a request from Ping, Pong emits exactly one reply to that same Ping.
observable_protocol.ping_behavior: When Ping consumes a reply from Pong, Ping emits exactly one next request to that same Pong.
observable_protocol.recurrence: After startup, the request/reply behavior repeats indefinitely without a protocol stop.

representation_policy.names: Target rebec, class, message-server, and package names are not semantic identifiers.
representation_policy.message_encoding: The source case objects may be represented by differently named typed Rebeca messages, provided direction, causality, multiplicity, and recurrence are preserved.
representation_policy.startup_encoding: Because Core Rebeca main cannot send messages directly, startup may be encoded by a constructor-triggered self-message or an auxiliary bootstrap rebec.
representation_policy.internal_steps: Protocol-neutral internal transitions are allowed between observable Ping/Pong sends, but they must not duplicate, drop, or reroute the logical protocol token.

excluded_from_equivalence: exact package qualification of message case objects
fairness stronger than the observed recurrent protocol

invariants.one_to_one_topology: One logical Ping communicates with one logical Pong.
invariants.reply_to_sender: Pong's reply returns to the Ping that sent the consumed request.
invariants.single_successor_message: A protocol handler produces exactly one next logical protocol message.
invariants.alternation: Observable protocol direction alternates Ping->Pong, Pong->Ping, Ping->Pong, ...
invariants.token_conservation: The recurrent protocol neither duplicates nor loses the single logical request/reply token.
invariants.nontermination: The intended protocol is recurrent; terminal quiescence is not a valid completed behavior.

tests.description: From initialization, logical Ping autonomously emits exactly one first request to logical Pong.
When logical Ping consumes a reply from Pong, it emits exactly one next request to the same Pong.
When logical Pong consumes a request from Ping, it emits exactly one reply to that same Ping.
No Ping/Pong protocol step emits more than one next cross-actor protocol message.
The recurrent protocol is between exactly one logical Ping role and one logical Pong role.
A connected execution from initialization contains initial Ping->Pong request followed by Pong->Ping reply.
A connected execution contains Ping->Pong request, Pong->Ping reply, and the next Ping->Pong request.
Within the recurrent protocol, request/reply steps preserve one logical token: no duplication and no cross-role loss are observed.
The state-space exposes one logical Ping and one logical Pong protocol role; auxiliary rebecs are ignored.
The protocol reaches its first Ping->Pong request from the generated model's initial state without semantic-test-harness intervention.
The reachable full state graph contains a cyclic strongly connected component with both Ping->Pong and Pong->Ping protocol progress.
After the recurrent protocol is entered, no reachable state inside the recurrent component is terminal/quiescent.
The complete scenario preserves automatic startup, one-to-one routing, one-request/one-reply alternation, token conservation, and recurrent nontermination.
